title: Heat & desert
about: Heat exhaustion and heatstroke, water in the heat, and travelling in hot dry places.

articles.title: Heat exhaustion and heatstroke
articles.intro: Heatstroke is an emergency. Cool first, then get help.
steps: Heat exhaustion: heavy sweating, weakness, headache, nausea, cramps. Move to shade, loosen clothes, sip water with salt and sugar, rest.
Heatstroke: very hot skin, confusion, fainting, fits, sometimes no sweating.
For heatstroke, cool them fast: shade, wet the skin and fan them, cold packs in armpits and groin, or soak in cool water.
Keep cooling until they're alert. Get medical help even if they recover.
avoid: Don't give drinks to someone who isn't fully awake.
Don't wait to see if heatstroke gets better on its own.

articles.title: Water in the heat
articles.intro: In hot weather you can lose more than a litre of sweat an hour.
steps: Plan at least 4 to 6 litres a day in desert heat, more when working.
Drink small amounts often. Add a pinch of salt and sugar (or ORS) on long hot days.
Travel early morning and evening; rest in shade at midday.
Cover up with loose, light clothes and a hat: it keeps more water in than bare skin.
avoid: Don't ration water to the point of feeling unwell: drink it, and find more.
Avoid alcohol and lots of caffeine.

articles.title: Lost in the heat
articles.intro: Stay put unless you know exactly where help is.
steps: Stay with your vehicle: it's easier to spot than a person.
Signal with a mirror, bright cloth or SOS on the ground. Send a BlueMob SOS.
Move only at night or early morning, and leave a note of your direction.
avoid: Don't walk off in the midday heat.
Don't drink radiator water or urine.
